'''Tamas I. Gombosi''' (born 1947) is a Hungarian space plasma physicist. He is the Konstantin I. Gringauz Distinguished University Professor of Space Science and Rollin M. Gerstacker Professor of Engineering at the [[University of Michigan]].

==Early life and education==
Gombosi was born in 1947<ref>{{cite web |title=Gombosi, Tamás, 1947- |url=http://viaf.org/viaf/92219647/#Gombosi,_Tam%C3%A1s_I. |publisher=[[VIAF]] |access-date=January 11, 2022}}</ref> in Budapest, Hungary<ref>{{cite web |title=Gombosi, Tamás I. |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n86862855.html |publisher=Library of Congress |access-date=January 11, 2022}}</ref> as the son of Hungarian [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] survivors.<ref name="Moore">{{cite web |last1=Casal Moore |first1=Nicole |title=Lecture offers a planetary scientist's tour through the solar system |url=https://news.engin.umich.edu/2015/02/lecture-offers-a-planetary-scientists-tour-through-the-solar-system/ |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=February 17, 2017}}</ref> He completed his graduate degrees in physics from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1970 and 1974 before conducting his postdoctoral research at the [[Russian Space Research Institute]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Tamas I. Gombosi |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/appliedphysics/people/faculty/tamas.html |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022}}</ref> While in Moscow, Gombosi worked on the [[Vener]] electron flux data with [[Konstantin Gringauz]]<ref name="Nagy">{{cite journal |last1=Nagy |first1=Andrew F. |title=A Career in Thin Air |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research|date=October 2019 |volume=124 |issue=10 |pages=7966–7970 |doi=10.1029/2019JA026777 |s2cid=203126123 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2019JGRA..124.7966N |hdl=2027.42/152475 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and was a member of the scientific staff of the Central Research Institute for Physics.<ref name="bio"/> While with the institute, Gombosi developed a better way to decode data during the Russian mission [[Interkosmos]] 3 and began to be mentored by [[Pavel Elyasberg]].<ref name="Moore"/> He remained in Moscow before being recruited by Andrew F. Nagy to join the faculty at the [[University of Michigan]] (UMich) in the late 1970s.<ref name="Nagy"/>

==Career==
Gombosi joined the faculty at UMich as a visiting scientist to work with Nagy on Pioneer Venus. He returned to Moscow before coming back to the United States permanently in 1983. Despite joining UMich, Gombosi remained involved in both the United States and [[Soviet Union]] space missions. Gombosi was involved in the [[Phobos program]] to Mars, the ''[[Cassini–Huygens]]'' mission to Saturn, the ''[[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta]]'' mission to comet 67P, and the [[STEREO]] mission to observe the Sun. His research team also developed a physics-based space weather-modeling framework that was adopted by the [[Space Weather Prediction Center]] to predict forecasts.<ref name="Moore"/> In the late 1990s, Gombosi led a research team in developing the first 3-D simulation of the Sun's [[heliosphere]], its upper atmosphere.<ref>{{cite web |title=3-D simulation of the sun's upper atmosphere |url=https://news.umich.edu/3-d-simulation-of-the-sun-s-upper-atmosphere/ |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=May 27, 1997}}</ref> Later, while serving as Chair of the Department of Atmospheric, Oceanic and Space Sciences, Gombosi led the effort for UMich to join the Department of Energy Fusion Science Center in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=U-M scientists part of new DOE-funded fusion science center |url=https://news.umich.edu/u-m-scientists-part-of-new-doe-funded-fusion-science-center/ |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=June 9, 2004}}</ref>

By 2014, Gombosi was serving as the Rollin M. Gerstacker Professor of Engineering, professor of atmospheric, oceanic and space sciences, professor of aerospace engineering, and director of the Center for Space Environment Modeling. The [[Rollin M. Gerstacker Foundation]] endowed and funded this professorship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Priebbe |first1=Melissa F |title=Gombosi Reappointed the Rollin M. Gerstacker Professor of Engineering |url=https://clasp.engin.umich.edu/2022/08/12/gombosi-reappointed-the-rollin-m-gerstacker-professor-of-engineering/ |website=umich.edu |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=26 August 2025}}</ref>   

As such, he was named the Konstantin I. Gringauz Distinguished University Professor of Space Science.<ref>{{cite web |title=Faculty members honored for scholarship, service |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/faculty-members-honored-scholarship-service/ |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=October 3, 2014}}</ref> Following this promotion, Gombosi was awarded the 2017 International Kristian Birkeland Medal for his "outstanding scientific results in the field of space weather."<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Gombosi receives International Kristian Birkeland Medal for work in space weather |url=https://clasp-archive.engin.umich.edu/articles/view/939#.Yd3cdNbMI3Q |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=November 9, 2018}}</ref> In 2020, Gombosi was awarded the John Adam Fleming Medal for "original research and technical leadership in geomagnetism, atmospheric electricity, aeronomy, space physics, and/or related sciences."<ref>{{cite web |title=Tamas I. Gombosi Receives 2020 John Adam Fleming Medal |url=https://eos.org/agu-news/tamas-i-gombosi-receives-2020-john-adam-fleming-medal |publisher=EOS |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=May 19, 2021}}</ref> The following year, Gombosi was appointed to the [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] Space Weather Advisory Group (SWAG).<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Gombosi named to new NOAA Space Weather Advisory Group |url=https://clasp.engin.umich.edu/2021/09/15/prof-gombosi-named-to-new-noaa-space-weather-advisory-group/ |publisher=University of Michigan |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=September 15, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gombosi and his wife Eszter, a Senior Programmer Analyst in the UMich Department of Biostatistics, have two children together.<ref name="bio"/>
